notes: This source/test traceability contract covers Umbra's bounded Request Retraction behavior for normal non-regional timestamped Send Interaction, Send Interaction With Regions, qualifying Update Attribute Values (including the bounded regional path), Send Directed Interaction, and non-regional timestamped Delete Object Instance in the non-installable IEEE 1516.1-2025 development profile. A federation-owned recipient ledger distinguishes pending from delivered fanout, including regional and directed interactions, timestamped attribute updates whose delivered nonconstrained recipient has no temporal-queue entry, and the deletion slice's mixed nonconstrained/time-constrained recipient set. Normal timestamped Send Interaction and a qualifying Update Attribute Values invocation—time-regulating with at least one TSO-preferred submitted attribute—now also allocate a valid designator when no recipient is eligible; their typed payload is immediately reclaimable while the ledger preserves legal Retract and terminal classification. A legal Retract uses the strict Clause 8.22.3 timestamp condition against the sender's current time or most recent advance-request time plus actual lookahead; it removes pending recipients and queues Request Retraction only for delivered recipients. The bounded lifecycle now separates a federation-owned lightweight terminal tombstone from typed payload: successful Retract, accepted producer TAR/TARA/NMR/NMRA/FQR requests, producer resignation, and an immediate actual-lookahead increase can terminalize a no-longer-retractable designator. Normal interaction/update/directed payload is released only after every still-joined pending recipient has crossed its callback boundary; deletion state is retained until both terminalization and pending-recipient drain, then its deleted-instance marker and name may be reclaimed. Terminal interaction and deletion regressions prove that an old designator remains MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted without dropping a queued callback or a reclaimable deletion name. Disable Time Regulation deliberately does not terminalize records because it removes Retract authority only while disabled. A focused normal-interaction regression now proves a live record remains intact through disable, pending re-enable, and the second regulation-enabled callback at unchanged lookahead, then supports legal Retract and normal terminal classification. A paired save/restore regression proves that a pre-save live normal-interaction record and its queued payload return after a post-save Retract terminalized them; the restored designator supports a legal post-delivery Retract and later terminal classification. A complementary save/restore regression saves an already terminal normal-interaction record and proves it restores as MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted while a distinct post-save handle remains invalid. Broader re-enable, save/restore, and cross-process lifetime matrices remain deferred. For the deletion slice, an execution-owned invocation snapshot restores the object/name/known state and committed ownership before that callback is exposed; a departed delivered recipient is correctly not notified or restored. A narrow save/restore regression additionally keeps TSO designator allocation monotonic, preventing a discarded post-save handle from aliasing fresh traffic after restore. The Requirements Lab's candidate export does not expose the complete strict-eligibility paragraphs as a standalone record; RL-019 records that source-span limitation, so the available service candidate is used only as a narrow anchor. Active in-flight ownership workflows, other producer/recipient resignation races, complete save/restore recovery, transport, package/catalog/JUnit/protected-review evidence, and conformance remain explicitly deferred.
